title: Worksheet — Lines and Angles (Class 6 CBSE)
instructions: Attempt all 10 questions. Use a protractor where needed. Show working for the subjective questions. Total time: 30 minutes.

questions.question: An angle is formed by:
options: two rays sharing a common endpoint
questions.answer: two rays sharing a common endpoint
questions.explanation: Two rays meeting at a common vertex form an angle.

questions.question: Vertically opposite angles formed by two intersecting lines are always equal.
An angle of 90° is called a ____ angle.
Two lines intersect; one angle is 70°. What is the angle directly opposite?
Explain in your own words the difference between a line, a line segment, and a ray.
questions.answer: A line extends without end in both directions and has no endpoints. A line segment is a piece of a line with two endpoints and a definite length. A ray has one endpoint and extends without end in the other direction.

questions.question: An angle has vertex P with arms going through K and L. List all valid names for this angle.
questions.answer: ∠KPL, ∠LPK, and ∠P (since only one angle has vertex P). The vertex P MUST be the middle letter when using three letters.

questions.question: Two lines intersect; one angle is 40°. Find the other three angles, naming the rule used.
questions.answer: Vertically opposite angle = 40° (vertically opposite are equal). Linear-pair partners = 180° − 40° = 140° each. Other three: 40°, 140°, 140°.
questions.explanation: Two key rules: vertically opposite equal; linear pair sums to 180°.

questions.question: Two lines intersect. The four angles around the intersection are labelled in order ∠1, ∠2, ∠3, ∠4. Given ∠1 = 65°, find each of ∠2, ∠3, ∠4 and state the rule used for each.
questions.answer: ∠2 (adjacent to ∠1) = 180° − 65° = 115° (linear pair). ∠3 (opposite ∠1) = 65° (vertically opposite). ∠4 (adjacent to ∠1) = 180° − 65° = 115° (linear pair). All four sum to 360°.
questions.explanation: Practises the rule used at each step.

questions.question: Find three angles around your home or classroom. Sketch each (or describe) and classify it as acute, right, obtuse, straight or reflex. Bonus: estimate the measure in degrees.
questions.answer: Example answers: (1) Corner of a notebook → 90° (right). (2) An open door at 45° from its frame → acute. (3) Hands of a clock at 4:00 → about 120° (obtuse). Many correct answers; rubric checks each angle has a sketch/description, classification, and a reasonable degree estimate.
